name: Mathura Ka Peda
instructions: 1. In a heavy-bottomed pan, cook full-fat milk on low heat while stirring continuously until it reduces into a thick Khoya.
2. Add ghee to the Khoya and roast it over low heat, stirring constantly until it turns a deep, rich brown color.
3. Add sugar and continue to cook until the sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens further.
4. Remove from heat and stir in green cardamom powder.
5. Allow the mixture to cool until it is warm enough to handle.
6. Add Bura (powdered sugar) for a traditional grainy texture and knead gently.
7. Shape the mixture into small, slightly flattened rounds and let them set before serving.
description: Mathura Ka Peda is a legendary sweet from the holy city of Mathura. Renowned for its unique dark brown color and caramelized, fudgy texture, it is considered an essential offering in local temples and a culinary symbol of the region's rich dairy heritage.
